Objective: Transition from the immediate survival of the forest journey to the logistical and emotional reality of rejoining the party, establishing the baseline for the intelligence exchange.
IntendedChange: Shift the narrative focus from external physical danger (Blight/Forest) to internal social dynamics and the weight of carried information, moving the party from a state of separation to a state of potential unity.
ProhibitedPatterns: Immediate combat or attack upon entering the watchfort
A new supernatural entity or voice appearing in the watchfort
Elias or Kaelen revealing the full strategic plan or the nature of the 'Key' in a monologue
The party immediately agreeing to a course of action without discussion
A cliffhanger ending where the gate closes or a new threat is spotted

Scenes.Purpose: Establish the physical and sensory contrast between the haunted forest and the mundane, worn reality of the watchfort, grounding the characters in safety.
Scenes.IntendedChange: Reduce tension from high-alert survival mode to cautious relief.

Scenes.Purpose: Reunite with the rest of the party, capturing the immediate emotional reaction of the group to seeing Elias and Kaelen alive and unharmed by the Blight.
Scenes.IntendedChange: Re-establish the social bonds and the collective relief of the group, validating the success of the journey.

Scenes.Purpose: Address the immediate physical needs of the group (wounds, exhaustion, hunger) to demonstrate the practical cost of the journey and the function of the watchfort as a refuge.
Scenes.IntendedChange: Shift focus from narrative momentum to character care and the tangible reality of their injuries.

Scenes.Purpose: Initiate the information exchange by presenting the physical evidence (the map, the gauntlet) rather than abstract concepts, allowing the party to react to the tangible artifacts.
Scenes.IntendedChange: Move the narrative from emotional reunion to intellectual engagement with the mystery.
